acceptance: The site-parity report shows 0 stale allowances on develop.
A decision is recorded on whether stale allowances fail the gate, and the gate or its docs match it.
context:
Seen in the site-parity job for #2669 (2026-10-05): 'summary: 0 missing path, 0 missing fragment, ... 36 stale allow'. The gate failure in that run was a separate docs-header focus bug, fixed in #2675.

Investigation 2026-10-06: the 36 entries are in known-broken-links.json and are reported by `site_inventory.py check` against the Astro candidate inventory (site-parity run on #2707, job 112096606186: 36 'no longer broken'). Separately, the gating Sphinx-vs-Astro diff reports 110 expected-removals-*.json patterns that 'matched nothing'; those belong to a different list and are out of this item's scope. Checking known-broken-links.json against the committed published baseline (_project/design/site-inventory/baseline-develop, the Sphinx site) reports 0 stale entries: all 66 entries, including the 36, are still broken links on the published Sphinx site. The same list is read by make site-inventory-check, scripts/site_deploy/gates.py (deploy link check) and scripts/site_parity.py. Production still renders with Sphinx (astro-site-53-cutover open). Pruning the 36 now would remove allowances for live broken links in production checks. They become stale only when production moves to Astro.

Decision (acceptance 2): stale allowances are reported, not failed, while one list serves both the Sphinx production site and the Astro candidate. The gate already behaves this way (site_inventory check lists them as informational 'stale allowance'; site_parity drops them from by_kind), so no gate or docs change is needed now. Revisit at the cutover: after Astro is production, prune the list against the production inventory and consider failing on stale entries then.

Blocked on astro-site-53-cutover. Next action (after cutover): run site_inventory.py check against the Astro production inventory, remove every entry reported 'no longer broken', and confirm 0 stale allowances in the site-parity job.
description: The site-parity report lists 36 "stale allowance" entries: links recorded as allowed breakage (missing paths on the blog index, missing fragments in several ADR, examples and API-reference pages) that are no longer broken. Stale entries hide nothing today, but they would silently re-allow those links if they broke again. Remove them from the allowed-differences inventory and decide whether a stale allowance should fail the gate instead of only being reported.
